entry_conditions: Use for the entire expanded carry/place/clear slice, not only an already-held object. Observed red starts include aligned open pickup with TCP z about 0.064-0.101 m; blue starts include z about 0.021-0.089 m. Fingers qpos[7:9] are about 0.040 m each before closing. Shared acquisition overlap includes closing fingers near 0.01825 m, lift and full-height carry. Already-held entry should provide two real causal observations showing object/TCP coupling when available; duplicated history cannot establish moving attachment. Fields are world-frame TCP pose 18:25, red 25:32, blue 32:39 (metres, wxyz), qpos 0:9, qvel 9:18, red goal 41:44 and blue goal 44:47. The model computes relative transforms in the TCP frame, but absolute Panda configuration and both world goal errors remain inputs. Open proximity alone is not attachment: the learned transform gate is suppressed without narrow fingers, proximity and two-frame movement evidence. These entry bands describe demonstrations, not validated contact or recovery limits. Forward has no selected/next tag argument: persistent red/blue tokens with red-to-blue and blue-to-none relations approximate the demonstrated role order, not arbitrary invocation assignments.
exit_conditions: A useful released-object state has the placed object's XY within a few millimetres of its own pad center in the observations, object z about 0.020 m, opening/open fingers approaching 0.040 m each and an empty TCP separating from the object. The demonstration command is g=+1 there; action sign is not itself an observed input or proof of release. After red, this policy also learns open retreat and return toward exposed blue, including a final descending approach band TCP z about 0.055-0.222 m with nonzero qvel. After blue it retains open retreat toward TCP z about 0.300 m and near-zero arm motion at the end. These are useful physical exit states, not added task predicates: the supplied contract requires only both objects' rotated XY containment and center-z tolerance, with no mandatory release, TCP clearance, speed or sustained hold.
overlap_role: Acquisition/carry overlap trains final open approach, closure and full lift before transport. The long red carry/blue acquisition overlap trains held descent to the red pad, release, empty retreat, lateral return and next-object approach. For example demo10200 overlaps acquire_lift on [80,180), [235,430) and [440,540); demo10204 uses [77,174), [230,418) and [434,532). All actions within this policy's 24 expanded slices retain ordinary diffusion supervision. Neither a first pad hit nor a transform discontinuity switches or deletes an object token. Both pad errors remain encoded during retreat and next approach. Causal finger aperture, TCP/object relative change, object height and goal error, TCP motion and qvel let the model distinguish supported transition states when taking over partway; two-frame stationary ambiguity remains a limitation.
successor_readiness: Blue acquisition can take control within the long overlap while red is still held/descending only if that successor supports completing red placement and release, or later with red stationary at its pad and an open empty gripper approaching exposed blue. Supply current world poses, both goals, qpos/qvel and the actual causal history, and tell the inference agent that red is previous and blue is next; this policy's neural forward itself cannot consume those external tags. A useful late handoff need not have zero velocity: demonstrated red endpoints are descending toward blue. Avoid treating red's geometric pad hit while fingers are still pinched as equivalent to an empty pickup-ready gripper. Final blue has no trained successor; both pad predicates may already hold before its open retreat finishes.
failure_signatures: Object-to-goal error failing to decrease while TCP-to-goal error decreases suggests an invalid grasp offset or failed coupling. Other warnings are an object following the TCP after apparent opening, fingers remaining pinched during motion toward blue, completed red leaving its pad during blue handling, or repeated high relative-transform change during claimed attachment. Confirm these using object/TCP motion across observations and finger aperture rather than proximity alone. A released object's transform will change as TCP retreats; that is expected separation, not evidence of a new valid grasp. The learned confidence is a weak moving-coupling estimate, not contact truth or slip recovery.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy through closing/lift/carry or the placed object's lowering, opening and clearance when physical transition completion is desired; do not terminate solely because TCP reaches a pad or an object first satisfies its geometric predicate. The model includes the post-red return toward blue, so continuation within the demonstrated expanded endpoint band is supported. Transfer to blue acquisition when the inference agent judges the observed overlap state suitable for that successor, not on a preset time schedule. If both task predicates already hold, the task contract can be satisfied immediately; final open retreat/settling is optional usability guidance rather than a redefinition of success. Do not rely on this model for unobserved recovery after the object is lost, role order is changed or the gripper drags a placed block. Host DDPM and eight-action execution cadence remain unchanged, with no custom replan controller.
limitations: Boundary/overlap ranges are measured training support, not policy performance, hard thresholds or guarantees. Finger aperture and two-frame rigidity infer attachment without force sensing. The conservative gate may be zero while a genuinely held object is stationary, and two observations cannot remember earlier attachment or exactly reproduce long stationary dwell timing. Explicit selected/next invocation tags are not in the supplied forward interface; both persistent object tokens avoid goal-hit reassignment but cannot guarantee external role persistence. Only small source/grasp offsets and nearly fixed rotations are represented in these demonstrations. No analytic IK/FK, image encoder, action equivariance, hard containment enforcement or scripted controller is implemented. Spatial/contact tolerances beyond these observations, arbitrary order, skew grasps, substantial slip and recovery remain unvalidated.
